glosses: Prétendre ouvertement à des actions ou des qualités.

examples.text: Christophe voudrait fanfaronner devant l'homme fort, mais sur ses joues sales ne savent que couler des larmes longues et tranchantes, telles des lames de faux.

Les quelques chasseurs de sangliers, d’authentiques Hurons des Maures qui se vantaient de connaître le moindre pouce de terrain, fanfaronnaient devant grand-mère : « Ne vous inquiétez pas, madame Burgaud, on vous le ramènera, votre mari. »

Lui, qui depuis toujours fanfaronnait que ses enfants étaient d’une intelligence très largement supérieure à la moyenne, était maintenant le premier à railler leurs hésitations, à s’agacer de leurs désirs et se moquer de leurs goûts.
Fallait qu'ils jactent, qu'ils fanfaronnent, qu'ils racontent tout fort leurs petites astuces cheloues, pour faire les malins. Et ça finissait toujours à leur désavantage, ces cons.
Devant les autres, je me vante, je fanfaronne : « Hé, tu n'as pas vu ce que j'ai fait cet été? Je me suis bâti une maison, un chalet, mon chalet. Tu devrais voir ça, c'est vraiment quelque chose. »
– Là, c’est l’île de Long Island. On va rentrer dans l’estuaire de l’Hudson River... fanfaronnait-il.

glosses: A brag; ostentatious positive appraisal of oneself.

examples.text: It was his regular boast that he could eat two full English breakfasts in one sitting.

glosses: A shot where the ball is driven off a side wall and then strikes the front wall.
To brag; to talk loudly in praise of oneself.

examples.text: On no account will he or any other kind be able to boast that he's escaped the pursuit of those who can follow so detailed and comprehensive a method of enquiry.

glosses: (used with \"about\" or \"of\") To speak of with pride, vanity, or exultation, with a view to self-commendation; to extol.

examples.text: Lest bad men should boast / Their specious deeds.

The dirty secret of the internet is that all this distraction and interruption is immensely profitable. Web companies like to boast about "creating compelling content", or offering services that let you "stay up to date with what your friends are doing",[…]and so on. But the real way to build a successful online business is to be better than your rivals at undermining people's control of their own attention.

glosses: To speak in exulting language of another; to glory; to exult.

examples.text: In God we boast all the day long.

glosses: To possess (a special and desirable quality).

examples.text: The hotel boasts one of the best views of the sea.
His family boasted a famous name.

Jinhua and others are spending big to get there. In Jinjiang, a city in Fujian Province once known as a shoe-manufacturing center, Jinhua’s new factory is almost finished. Rising five stories and stretching several football fields long, the structure boasts 100,000 square feet of new office space.
After dropping off travellers at Foregate Street, my train terminates at Shrub Hill - a station which boasts one of the best selection [sic] of semaphore signals left in the country.

glosses: To dress, as a stone, with a broad chisel.
To shape roughly as a preparation for the finer work to follow; to cut to the general form required.
To behave (especially to walk or carry oneself) in a pompous, superior manner.

examples.text: What hempen home-ſpuns haue we ſwaggering here, / So neere the Cradle of the Faierie Queene?

glosses: To boast or brag noisily; to bluster; to bully.

examples.text: To be great is not […] to swagger at our footmen.

For the common Soldier when he goes to the Market or Ale-house will offer this Money, and if it be refused, perhaps he will SWAGGER and HECTOR, and Threaten to Beat the BUTCHER or Ale-Wife, or take the Goods by Force, and throw them the bad HALF-PENCE.

glosses: To walk with a swaying motion.

examples.text:
It's the injustice… he is so unjust—
whiskey-blind, swaggering home at five.

glosses: Someone carrying a swag; a swagman.

examples.text: There were now more swaggers passing down Ferry Street and more coming to ask for food […].
